D010_l001.question: An 82-year-old widowed female, residing in a nursing home, presents with a complex psychiatric history spanning several months. She reports a 1-month period characterized by an irritable mood, psychomotor agitation, and pressured speech. During this time, she experienced an inability to control her thoughts and sustained difficulty with attention, leading to significant functional impairment. Concurrent with this period, the patient endorsed gustatory hallucinations. This was preceded by a 4-month episode marked by a pervasive loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities, significant weight loss exceeding 5% of her body weight, and initial insomnia. She also exhibited psychomotor retardation in her speech, a marked loss of energy preventing daily activities, and delusional guilt. During this episode, she reported sudden, strong suicidal impulses without specific plans.
D010_l001.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D010_l001.answer: A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010_l002.question: A 32-year-old single male archivist presents with a history of mood disturbances. For one month, he exhibited an abnormally elevated and euphoric mood, accompanied by significant psychomotor agitation, incessant talkativeness, and racing thoughts. His attention was notably drawn to extraneous stimuli. During this period, he also experienced visual hallucinations. This constellation of symptoms resulted in significant functional impairment. Preceding this, for a duration of four months, the patient experienced a period characterized by indifference to achievements, decreased appetite, and non-restorative sleep. He displayed psychomotor retardation, reported a profound loss of energy, and harbored feelings of worthlessness, including sudden suicidal impulses without a specific plan. This depressive phase also led to marked functional impairment.
D010_l002.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D010_l002.answer: A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010_l003.question: A 40-year-old single female, employed as a hotel manager, presents with a complex psychiatric history. For the past month, she has exhibited mood lability, psychomotor agitation, pressured speech, racing thoughts, and severely impaired attention, all of which significantly impact her occupational functioning. During this period, she also reported tactile hallucinations. Prior to this, for a duration of four months, she experienced a distinct depressive episode characterized by anhedonia, significant weight gain, initial insomnia, psychomotor retardation with slowed speech, profound loss of energy leading to functional impairment, and delusional guilt. This depressive episode was complicated by a suicide attempt. Her current presentation is marked by the presence of psychotic symptoms exclusively during the manic phase.
D010_l003.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D010_l003.answer: A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010_l004.question:
A 25-year-old single male delivery driver presents with a complex psychiatric history spanning approximately five months. For one month, he exhibited a distinct period of elevated mood characterized by marked mood lability, rapidly fluctuating between euphoria and irritability. During this time, he experienced significantly increased energy, rapid and pressured speech that was difficult to interrupt, and an inability to control his racing thoughts. His attention was easily drawn to trivial external stimuli. This period was also notable for the presence of tactile hallucinations, described as sensations of touch or movement on his skin without an apparent external stimulus. These symptoms resulted in functional impairment.

This manic presentation was preceded by a four-month period of significant depression. During this depressive phase, the patient exhibited prominent social withdrawal, a 5% unintentional weight loss within one month, and recurrent distressing nightmares. He also presented with psychomotor retardation affecting his speech, manifesting as long response latencies and slowed verbal output. Physical fatigue was pronounced, and he endorsed a passive wish to die without active suicidal ideation. Notably, he reported delusional levels of guilt, feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events. His depressive symptoms also led to significant functional impairment.
D010_l004.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D010_l004.answer: A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010_l005.question: A 33-year-old single male film editor presents with a complex psychiatric history. He reports a four-month period of depressive symptoms, characterized by profound indifference to personal achievements, decreased appetite, and non-restorative sleep. During this time, he experienced significant loss of energy leading to functional impairment, psychomotor agitation, delusional guilt, and suicidal ideation without a specific plan. This depressive episode was preceded by a one-month duration of elevated mood, heightened psychomotor activity, and pressured speech, also causing functional impairment. During this elevated mood phase, he reported a flooding of thoughts, marked responsiveness to extraneous stimuli, and visual hallucinations.
D010_l005.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010_l006.question: A 32-year-old married male sales representative presents with a two-month history of a significant shift in mood and behavior. He exhibits a predominantly irritable mood, characterized by increased anger and aggression in response to minor stimuli. Psychomotor agitation is notable, with the patient describing an inability to tolerate rest and a constant drive to engage in activities. His speech is rapid and difficult to interrupt, making communication challenging, and he reports persistent racing thoughts, with ideas quickly escalating and shifting. The patient also reports a marked increase in sexual interest and activity (hypersexuality). During this period, he experiences referential delusions, believing that ordinary events and remarks hold special significance for him. Concurrently, he reports visual hallucinations, perceiving individuals and objects that are not present. These symptoms collectively have led to marked functional impairment.
D010_l006.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D010_l006.answer: A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010_l007.question: A 41-year-old male, married and working as a bus driver, presents with a two-month history of a distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated mood. Socially, he has been significantly more gregarious and extroverted than his baseline. These symptoms have led to significant functional impairment.

    B. Bipolar I Disorder

D010_l009.question:

D010_l011.question:
A 56-year-old male truck driver, divorced for several years, presents with a three-week history of elevated mood and increased energy. His speech was notably pressured and excessive, and he described a racing and disorganized stream of thoughts. Concurrent with these symptoms, he reported gustatory hallucinations, experiencing tastes that were not present. These symptoms resulted in significant functional impairment.

Prior to this presentation, for a duration of three months, the patient experienced a persistently depressed mood, characterized by anhedonia and a notable indifference to his achievements. During this depressive episode, he engaged in a suicide attempt, leading to considerable functional impairment.

    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D010_l013.question:

D010_l021.question: A 38-year-old single male, employed as a tattoo artist, presents with a three-month history of significant mood and behavioral disturbances.
